title: Quarantine, Archive, Restore, Purge
objective: Introduce reversible lifecycle operations before expanding autonomy.

stories.title: Quarantine store semantics
stories.outcome: Define same-volume move-first quarantine with explicit capacity and boundary checks.
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine never copies huge data when atomic/same-volume move is required by policy.
Insufficient space or cross-volume uncertainty fails closed.
Original identity and restore metadata are recorded contentlessly.
verification: Cross-volume, full-disk, rename-failure, and crash-injection tests.

stories.title: Restore protocol
stories.outcome: Restore quarantined artifacts only if destination safety and conflict policy are satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Restore never overwrites unrelated current provider state silently.
Conflict outcomes are explicit: refuse, alternate location, or provider-specific restore.

stories.title: Archive/compression lifecycle
stories.outcome: Support cold archival for eligible artifacts with verifiable archive integrity.
stories.risk_reclassification_note: Declared CR3 at planning time; raised to CR4 at implementation because the change adds a new mutation capability (MutationOperation::Archive) inside rust/crates/cancellai-platform/src/mutation.rs, the sole SI-019 mutation-boundary seam - the commit-time risk-floor gate refused the CR3 declaration on exactly this path floor.
acceptance_criteria: Compression never changes semantic classification to disposable.
Restore integrity is checked before source purge.

stories.title: Purge and tombstones
stories.outcome: Permanently purge only within authority ceilings and preserve a minimal contentless tombstone.
stories.ac_narrowing_note: AC1 originally read 'Tombstones contain no prompts/source/file contents' as an unqualified guarantee. Two independent review rounds established that no local, orchestrator-less primitive can prove that property for a caller-supplied required identifier field - a finite character/shape predicate cannot distinguish a real ID from a short ordinary phrase re-encoded to look like one (round 2's own finding, `do-not-purge-this`). ADR-0033 narrows AC1, by owner decision, to the testable property below: no descriptive annotation fields at all, and a disclosed (not closed) residual for the three structurally required linkage fields, deferred to a future orchestrator story.
acceptance_criteria: Tombstones carry no descriptive annotation fields (provider_id/category/reason_code/policy_id are absent, not merely validated); artifact_id/plan_id/evidence_ids are each validated as a short, identifier-shaped value, rejecting an obvious prompt/source/path - this is a disclosed residual against arbitrary short phrases, not a closed guarantee (ADR-0033).
Irreversible purge is distinguishable from vendor-native conditionally reversible operations.
verification: Privacy field allowlist test, purge evidence tests, direct-ledger-bypass regression test, and a deliberately-passing disclosed-residual test.
